LESSON: LEADERSHIP IN ISRAEL

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible 3.2 Divisions of the Bible (6 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, 
Topic 3.4: Leadership in Israel

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Leadership in Israel. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why was leadership in Israel important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel
2. identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus
3. apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives
4. value responsibility by choosing credible leaders

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LEADERSHIP IN ISRAEL
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Leadership in Israel helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: LEADERSHIP IN ISRAEL
Study Leadership in Israel like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Leadership in Israel” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Leadership in Israel in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives

What this means
In this part you learn to apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Value responsibility by choosing credible leaders

What this means
In this part you learn to value responsibility by choosing credible leaders. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value responsibility by choosing credible leaders.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Leadership in Israel” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value responsibility by choosing credible leaders. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Leadership in Israel is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Leadership in Israel” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Leadership in Israel in your own words. (skill: identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives)

Example 4: Show how “Leadership in Israel” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: value responsibility by choosing credible leaders)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Leadership in Israel to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel.
3. Practise this skill: identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus.
4. Practise this skill: apply leadership qualities learnt from Moses in their daily lives.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Leadership in Israel from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Leadership in Israel: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Leadership in Israel?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why was leadership in Israel important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Leadership in Israel means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe how God prepared Moses for leadership in Israel.
5. Be able to: identify the roles played by Moses during the Exodus.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
